o1.biggest_strength: The forecast is broken out by cause, not topic: it separates Simplify-debts tickets from other balance tickets, puts a different, justified share on each, and carries the arithmetic all the way to dollars — and the three articles are genuinely publishable, with app and web steps and real cancellation steps for Apple and Google.
o1.biggest_mistake: It proposes merging a 71%-helpful article ('Recording a payment') on no evidence of duplication, which risks breaking the one thing that works, and it leads with a single optimistic 3,743 / 21% number instead of a range I could defend upward.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Present the forecast as a low-to-high range with each share tied to something in the data, drop or heavily caveat the merge, and add a short 'what to watch next month' so I can tell whether it worked.

o2.biggest_strength: It answers the actual question in the first three lines — three articles, five links, 11% to 22% — then says plainly that nothing needs merging because the problem is findability, not duplication, and defends a conservative range that leaves currency and merging as upside.
o2.biggest_mistake: It applies one flat 25%–50% band to three different mechanisms and props it up with a comparison that isn't quite right (50% is not below the 38% 'did this help' rate), and the restore article has no web steps even though the searches come from both.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Differentiate the shares by topic with a sentence each on why, add splitwise.com steps to the restore article, and suggest the inline 'Balances are simplified. Why?' link on the balances screen rather than only the Help link.

reason: I'd send both to the team, but I'd send #2 first: it opens with the decision and a range I can defend upward, and it leaves the 71%-helpful payment article alone. #1 goes deeper on the forecast and writes more complete articles, but its merge idea and its 21% headline would need softening before I'd repeat them to anyone.
